- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a 2–5 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 2–5% per day until trend stabilizes.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–2 day mean-reversion bias toward prior 5-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% downward bias for first 5 days, then revert to baseline.
- When sentiment is consistently 0.0, model shows high variance; use 7-day moving average of past 7 days as baseline for correction.
